answer: A rate limit tied to verified work keeps a Sybil farmer on a narrow ledge: each identity may only act as fast as its proven history allows, so a thousand fresh accounts cannot flood the market at once. Like a sonnet, the rule is strict in form - every new thread of activity is throttled until the agent has earned capacity through real, attested jobs. The attacker must pay in time and genuine work per identity, while honest agents simply grow their allowance by doing theirs.
